info.title: hexaeight-activate — HexaEight identity activation CLI
info.description: Command-line tool for HexaEight identities on this machine: install the official agent (downloaded from GitHub and hash-verified against a value shipped inside this package), activate a machine token, renew it, verify the licence, check that the HexaEight libraries an agent is running match the packages published on nuget.org, and control which agent builds an identity accepts messages from. Subcommands: install-agent, newtoken (default), renewtoken, cpucores, verify-env, verify-libs, approve-builds.

commands.name: cpucores
commands.description:
Print the CPU and core count this machine reports.
Your HexaEight license must cover at least this many cores.

commands.name: install-examples
commands.description:
Put a small local model on this machine, point the agent at
it, and write runnable examples. No API key and no account —
it exists so a fresh install can do something immediately.
Not for production; bring a provider key for real work.
--dir PATH      install somewhere other than here
--model-only    skip the example files

commands.name: install-router
commands.description:
Download the official LLM router for this platform and
verify it. The router fronts your model providers, so the
agents calling it never hold a provider key.
--dir PATH  install somewhere other than the current folder

commands.name: newtoken
commands.description:
Interactive activation (default if no command is given).
Prompts for resource name, password, license code,
and a QR-code approval from the HexaEight Authenticator app.
Writes env-file and hexaeight.mac to the current directory.
On success, runs a quick license verification automatically.

commands.name: Notes
commands.description:
- Run from the directory where you want env-file and hexaeight.mac
to be written (typically your application's working directory).
- For the Azure Marketplace VM activation path, see the docs at
hexaeight.com/docs.

commands.name: renewtoken
commands.description:
Renew an existing license. Prompts for the new
license code received by email after purchase.
Updates HEXAEIGHT_MACHINETOKEN in env-file.
On success, runs a quick license verification automatically.

commands.name: verify-env
commands.description:
Run a license verification — encrypt and decrypt a random
probe message locally to confirm the activation is healthy.
Then check the agent's libraries, as verify-libs does.

options.name: --restore
options.description: replace any that do not match

options.name: --dir
options.description:
check a specific folder
Exit: 0 all match, 1 a mismatch, 2 nothing found to check.

commands.name: verify-libs
commands.description:
Check the HexaEight libraries this machine's agent is running
against the packages published on nuget.org. No license call,
so it is cheap enough to run on a schedule.
--restore   replace any that do not match
--dir PATH  check a specific folder
Exit: 0 all match, 1 a mismatch, 2 nothing found to check.
